recent.task: Running pace calculator: distance and time give pace per km and per mile and projected times for 5 km, 10 km, half, and full marathon.
Weekly planner page with priorities, appointments, and notes, printable on A4.
CV checklist: 15 checks with a score, printable.
Water tracker: a daily goal the user sets and a tap-to-add log that resets each day.
Stretch sequence timer: the user lists stretches and hold times, and the timer runs through them.
Weekly workout planner: days, exercises, sets, and reps, printable.
Goal tracker: one goal with milestones, dates, and percent done.
Camping checklist grouped by shelter, cooking, clothing, and safety, printable.
Daily routine builder: morning and evening steps with times, printable.
Output style: a Claude Code voice that changes how every answer sounds.
Plugin: a bundle of Claude Code mods that arrives like a traveller with a full pack.
Long task: a Claude Code job that runs for hours while no one watches.
Loop: Claude Code waking on a schedule to check on something again and again.
Session log: the trail a Claude Code session leaves behind it.
Mod workshop: a place to build a Claude Code mod from parts.
Companion: a Claude Code mod that keeps someone company while they work.
Scroll progress: a thin line that shows how much of a page is read.
Undo in rewind: a mistake runs back along its own path, the way tape plays in reverse.
Color swatch in dye bath: dip the cloth, and it slowly takes one color from a small set of vats.
Badge in droplets: the count grows as drops merge, and a drop splits off when it goes down.
File drop in a well: a dropped file falls, rings spread, and the echo confirms it arrived.
Empty state in tide pool: an empty list is a still pool with one small creature waiting.
Breadcrumb in footprints: the trail back up is a line of prints that deepen as each is reached.
Log viewer: a compact panel for a developer tool that filters sample events by severity and opens the selected event details.
Pipeline panel: a status panel for a build tool that expands a failed step, shows its log and retries it in a local demo.
Latency chart: a chart card for a service dashboard that selects a time range and reveals request latency at a chosen point.

components.name: Range selector
components.description: Segmented radio group for 1h, 6h, 24h and 7d with fixed label widths.
components.purpose: Choose the time window the card reads.
components.use: Engineer widens from 6h to 24h to see whether a spike repeats daily.
components.input: Click or tap a segment. Keyboard: Tab into the group, arrow keys move and select, Home and End jump to the ends.
components.outcome: Range commits and emits one load request. Selecting the active range emits nothing.
components.recovery: If the load is cancelled or fails, the selection reverts to the last range that loaded.
components.mechanism: Native radio inputs styled as segments. A generation counter tags each request. Older generations are ignored on arrival.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-26 log viewer severity filter. That filter narrows a list. This control replaces the whole data window and must abort prior work.
components.usefulness: Every latency question starts with a window. Without dedupe, rapid clicks queue several loads.
components.creativeDifference: Revert-on-cancel keeps control and chart in agreement, which a plain segmented control does not handle.
states: idle: one range checked, reached on load
focus: visible ring on checked segment, reached by Tab
pending: checked segment shows a 2px underline while its load runs, reached by selecting a new range
reverted: previous range re-checked with status text 'Kept 6h', reached by cancel or failure
no-op: active range pressed again, nothing changes

components.name: Load stages
components.description: Status line that names three load stages, allows cancel and ends in a clear complete or failed state.
components.purpose: Show what the card is doing while data loads, and how it ended.
components.use: Engineer sees 'Aggregating 864 samples' and decides to wait or cancel.
components.input: Click or tap Cancel or Retry. Keyboard: Tab to the button, Enter or Space.
components.outcome: Stages Fetch, Aggregate and Draw tick in order. Completion reads 'Loaded 24h · 288 points · 14:52'.
components.recovery: Cancel keeps the previous chart. Failure names the stage that failed and offers one Retry that disables while pending.
components.mechanism: A single job object with an AbortController and stage index. Starting a job aborts the current one. Status text sits in a polite live region. No percentage is shown, because stage count is the honest measure.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-27 pipeline panel retry. That panel retries a build step. This one reports a data load with cancel and never shows invented progress.
components.usefulness: Engineers need to know whether a flat line means low latency or no data yet.
components.creativeDifference: Named stages with sample counts replace a spinner, so the wait carries information.
states: idle: hidden status, reached when no load is running
fetching: 'Fetching 24h', reached by range change
aggregating: 'Aggregating 864 samples', reached after fetch resolves
drawing: 'Drawing p99', reached after aggregate
complete: summary line with timestamp, reached after draw
cancelled: 'Cancelled · kept 6h', reached by Cancel
failed: 'Aggregate failed · kept 6h' with Retry, reached by demo failure toggle
reduced-motion: stage ticks without transition

sources.title: Engineering-leaning charts and UI components (visitor request)

components.name: Percentile tiles
components.description: Four tiles for p50, p95, p99 and error rate. The selected tile expands while neighbours yield track space.
components.purpose: Pick which series the chart plots and show current values for all four.
components.use: Engineer switches from p99 to p50 to check whether the median moved too.
components.input: Click or tap a tile. Keyboard: Tab to a tile, Enter or Space selects.
components.outcome: Selected tile expands to show its detail. The chart redraws in that series.
components.recovery: Selecting another tile reverses the change. Nothing is lost.
components.mechanism: rAF loop eases CSS fr track variables with k = 1 - (1 - 0.14)^dt, dt capped at 50 ms. The loop stops when the summed error drops below 0.002. Below 480 px container width, tiles become a chip row with no track animation.
components.nearestAnalogue: None in recent dates. Source c16 magnetic bento is the direct ancestor.
components.usefulness: Percentile choice changes what a spike means. Current values for all four stay visible.
components.creativeDifference: Track yielding ties layout to selection, while values stay readable during resize.
states: default: p99 selected, reached on load
selected: expanded track with detail and accent border, reached by click or Enter
focus: outline ring, reached by Tab
settled: loop stopped, reached about 400 ms after selection
compact: chip row under 480 px container width
reduced-motion: tracks set directly

sources.title: Stop Treating CSS Container Queries Like Traditional Media Queries

components.name: Cursor chart
components.description: SVG line chart with an SLO line and a cursor that snaps to measured samples and reveals the value at that point.
components.purpose: Reveal request latency at a chosen point.
components.use: Engineer drags across the deploy and reads '14:35 · p99 640 ms · +340 over SLO'.
components.input: Pointer move or touch drag over the plot. Keyboard: focus the plot, Left and Right step one sample, Page Up and Page Down step 12, Home and End jump to the ends.
components.outcome: Readout above the plot shows time, value and offset from SLO. Cursor snaps to the nearest real sample.
components.recovery: Escape returns the cursor to the worst breach. Leaving the plot keeps the last cursor position.
components.mechanism: Nearest-index lookup from x position against sample timestamps. Readout has fixed width from the longest sample label. Plot is a focusable element with role group and an aria-live readout.
components.nearestAnalogue: None in recent dates. 2026-10-19 scroll progress maps position to value in one dimension, with no data points.
components.usefulness: This component answers the core need. Snapping prevents reading interpolated values that were never measured.
components.creativeDifference: The readout states distance from SLO, which reframes the number as a decision.
states: initial: cursor on worst breach, reached on load
tracking: cursor follows pointer, reached by pointer or touch
focus: plot outline and key hint, reached by Tab
breach: readout marked over SLO, reached when value exceeds 300 ms
stale: dimmed plot while a new range loads
empty: 'No samples in range', reached when a range returns zero points

sources.title: Engineering-leaning charts and UI components (visitor request)

components.name: Breach stepper
components.description: Previous and next controls that move the chart cursor between SLO breaches, with a count.
components.purpose: Move directly between moments where latency crossed the SLO.
components.use: Engineer steps 'Breach 2 of 4' to 'Breach 3 of 4' to see whether the second spike followed a deploy.
components.input: Click or tap Previous or Next. Keyboard: Tab to the buttons, Enter or Space. Held keys move one step per keydown.
components.outcome: Cursor jumps to the peak sample of the next breach. Count updates.
components.recovery: The buttons disable at the ends, and the count reads 'Breach 4 of 4'. Escape in the chart returns to the worst breach.
components.mechanism: Breaches are contiguous runs above SLO, computed once per load. Each run is stored by its peak index. A step sets the cursor index directly and replaces any running transition.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-25 breadcrumb in footprints moves through a path. This moves through computed events in data.
components.usefulness: Finding breaches by dragging across 288 points is slow on a phone.
components.creativeDifference: Navigation targets come from the data itself, not from pages or sections.
states: default: 'Breach 1 of 4', reached on load
middle: both buttons enabled
start or end: one button disabled with count at bound
none: 'No breaches in 1h' with both disabled, reached when range has none
focus: visible ring

sources.title: Engineering-leaning charts and UI components (visitor request)

components.name: Pin pair
components.description: Button that pins the cursor point. Two pins produce a delta line.
components.purpose: Keep two moments and compare them.
components.use: Engineer pins 14:15 and 14:35 and reads '+412 ms p99 over 20 min'.
components.input: Click or tap Pin. Keyboard: Tab to Pin, Enter or Space. P while the chart has focus. Each pin chip has a remove button.
components.outcome: First pin shows a marker. Second pin shows the delta line. A third pin replaces the oldest.
components.recovery: Remove any pin with its x button or Delete on the focused chip. Pinning an already pinned point does nothing.
components.mechanism: A two-slot array keyed by sample index. The label swaps in a reserved width: Pin, Pinned, Replace oldest.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-20 undo in rewind deals with reversal of an action. This keeps two references and computes between them.
components.usefulness: Before and after a deploy is the comparison on-call engineers report.
components.creativeDifference: The delta is the action's result, so no separate compare panel is needed.
states: empty: 'Pin this point'
one pinned: marker on chart, label 'Pin second point'
pair: delta line shown
full: label 'Replace oldest'
duplicate: label 'Already pinned', no change
cleared: pins removed on range change, with status note

recent.task: Import progress: a loader for a file tool that shows named stages, lets someone cancel and ends with a clear completion state.

components.name: Choose files empty state
components.description: Empty import zone with one action and a drop target.
components.purpose: Start an import when nothing is chosen.
components.use: A designer opens Import and picks brand-kit.zip.
components.input: Click or tap Choose files, or drop files onto the zone. Keyboard: Tab to the button, then Enter or Space opens the native file picker.
components.outcome: The chosen files are counted ('14 files · 3.2 MB') and the import starts.
components.recovery: Closing the picker without a choice leaves the empty state unchanged. A drop with zero files reads 'Nothing dropped' and keeps the button focused.
components.mechanism: A native input type=file sits behind a visible button. Drop is handled by dragover and drop listeners on the zone. Pointer is not required, because the button covers every path.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-24 empty state in tide pool and 2026-10-23 file drop in a well. Both are animated scenes. This is a static zone with one labelled action.
components.usefulness: It gives one obvious way in and meets the one-action constraint.
components.creativeDifference: The drop target and the button are the same element, so touch users without drag lose nothing.
states: empty: button 'Choose files', reached on load and after a cancel with nothing placed
drag-over: dashed border turns solid with text 'Drop to import', reached by dragging files over the zone
focus: 2px ring on the button, reached by Tab
nothing-dropped: note under the button, reached by an empty drop

components.name: Import stage track
components.description: Four named stages with real file counts and a small arc on the active stage only.
components.purpose: Show which stage is running and how many files it has handled.
components.use: A designer reads 'Convert · 7 of 13' and decides to wait.
components.input: Display only. Keyboard: the track is skipped in tab order, and its live region is announced by screen readers.
components.outcome: Read, Check, Convert and Place advance in order. Each completed stage shows a tick glyph and its final count.
components.recovery: On cancel or failure, the track freezes at the stage reached and names it ('Stopped at Convert').
components.mechanism: A job object holds the stage index and per-stage counters. The source's rotating top-border arc is drawn at 14px on the active stage. Glyphs and text change on each tick, and the live region throttles announcements to stage changes plus every fifth file. No percentage is shown.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-28 load stages. That row has three fixed stages with sample counts. This row counts discrete files per stage and records where a cancel happened.
components.usefulness: File counts are the honest measure of an import, so the wait carries information.
components.creativeDifference: State is shown by glyph shape and bold text, so it survives greyscale. The arc is the only motion.
states: idle: hidden, reached before any files are chosen
reading: 'Read · 14 files', reached when files are chosen
checking: 'Check · 1 unsupported', reached after read
converting: 'Convert · n of 13', reached after check
placing: 'Place · n of 12', reached after convert
complete: all ticks, reached after place
stopped: hollow glyph and 'Stopped at <stage>', reached by Cancel or demo failure
reduced-motion: static arc and the word 'running'

components.name: Cancel import
components.description: A thumb-height cancel button that stops the job and rolls back any placed files.
components.purpose: Stop an import in flight and leave the canvas as it was.
components.use: A designer sees the wrong zip in the read count and cancels.
components.input: Click or tap Cancel import (44px tall, full width at the panel's foot). Keyboard: Tab to it and press Enter or Space, or press Escape anywhere in the panel.
components.outcome: The job aborts. Any layers placed in this run are removed, and replaced layers return.
components.recovery: After cancelling, the panel returns to the row 1 empty state. A repeated press while cancelling is ignored.
components.mechanism: An AbortController is passed to every stage. A placed-layer list is kept for the run and reversed on abort. The label swaps within a reserved width: Cancel import, Cancelling, Cancelled.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-28 load stages cancel, which kept the previous chart. This cancel also rolls back partial canvas changes.
components.usefulness: Imports change user work, so stopping halfway must not leave half a kit on the canvas.
components.creativeDifference: Escape and a bottom-edge target give the same reach to keyboard and thumb.
states: ready: enabled during any running stage
pressed: sinks 1px with a reduced shadow, reached on pointer down or key down
cancelling: disabled with label 'Cancelling', reached on press
cancelled: 'Cancelled at Convert · canvas unchanged', reached after rollback
hidden: not rendered when idle or complete
focus: 2px ring

components.name: File manifest
components.description: Per-file list showing each file's state with shape glyphs and a short reason.
components.purpose: Show what happened to each file.
components.use: A designer finds that ad-banner.psd was skipped as an unsupported type.
components.input: Click or tap a row to expand its reason. Keyboard: Tab into the list, Up and Down move between rows, Home and End jump, Enter expands.
components.outcome: The expanded row shows type, size and reason ('Unsupported type .psd', 'Replaces layer hero-photo').
components.recovery: Collapsing a row with Enter or a second tap returns it to one line. Selection persists across stage updates.
components.mechanism: A listbox with roving tabindex. Rows update in place by file id, so the order never jumps. Glyphs are a hollow circle (queued), a filled circle (placed), a slashed circle (skipped) and a double ring (replaced), each paired with a word.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-26 log viewer event list. That list filters past events. This one updates live per file and carries outcome reasons.
components.usefulness: A summary count alone hides which file failed and why.
components.creativeDifference: Each state has its own shape and word, so the list reads in greyscale.
states: queued: hollow glyph, reached on read
working: bold row text, reached when the file's stage runs
placed: filled glyph
replaced: double ring with the layer name
skipped: slashed glyph with reason
expanded: detail line, reached by Enter or tap
focus: row ring, reached by arrows

components.name: Import summary
components.description: Completion card with grouped counts, skip reasons and one next action.
components.purpose: End the import with a clear statement of what landed.
components.use: A designer reads 'Imported 12 of 14 · 3 replaced · 2 skipped · 14:52'.
components.input: Click or tap Show skipped to jump to the manifest rows. Keyboard: Tab to the link and press Enter. Focus moves to the summary heading on completion.
components.outcome: The counts are grouped by placed, replaced and skipped. The placed files settle into the canvas tray once at 180ms ease-out.
components.recovery: If nothing was placed, the card reads 'Nothing imported' and offers a single 'Choose other files' action.
components.mechanism: The summary is rendered once from the final job record. Focus moves to an h2 with tabindex=-1. The tray settle is one transform transition and is skipped under reduced motion.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-28 load stages completion line. That was one line. This row groups outcomes and links to the skipped files.
components.usefulness: It gives the visitor a definite end, with no ambiguity between done and stuck.
components.creativeDifference: The landing motion carries the Puppet maker's frame break into the editor once, then stops.
states: complete: all files placed
complete-with-skips: counts plus a Show skipped link
nothing-imported: one action 'Choose other files'
undone: struck summary with 'Undone at 14:53', reached by row 6
reduced-motion: no tray settle

components.name: Undo import
components.description: Undo button that reverses a finished import and names the layers that came back.
components.purpose: Reverse a completed import and show what was restored.
components.use: A designer undoes the import and reads 'Restored logo-mark, hero-photo, headline · removed 12'.
components.input: Click or tap Undo import. Keyboard: Tab to it and press Enter or Space, or press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS) while the editor has focus.
components.outcome: Imported layers are removed and the 3 replaced layers return in their original order. The restored names are listed and briefly outlined on the canvas.
components.recovery: Redo import (Ctrl+Shift+Z) reapplies the same import. A second undo with an empty history does nothing and reads 'Nothing to undo'.
components.mechanism: One history entry per import stores the removed layer snapshots and the added layer ids. Undo swaps them as one operation. The label swaps within a reserved width: Undo import, Undone, Redo import.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-20 undo in rewind, which animated a mistake playing backward. This undo is instant and names what returned.
components.usefulness: An import that silently replaces layers needs a way back that says what it restored.
components.creativeDifference: The result is a named list of what came back. Restoration is reported, not implied.
states: available: enabled after complete
pressed: 1px sink with a reduced shadow
undone: restored names listed and the label set to 'Redo import'
redone: summary returns to complete
empty-history: disabled with 'Nothing to undo'
focus: 2px ring

popularSnapshot.method: Live Popular collection, 12 results; first three rendered cards in ranked order. Displayed score includes the site's implicit +1; not raw vote totals. Snapshot reused for both experiment nights, not claimed as a fresh ranking at run time.
